identity.title: OpenThoughts: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models

problem.claim: The project seeks to create open-source datasets for training reasoning models.

gap.claim: The best training recipes remain uncertain because leading reasoning models often depend on proprietary datasets with little public information.

contributions.claim: Introduces the OpenThoughts2-1M and OpenThoughts3 open reasoning-data datasets, with datasets and models made available publicly.
Reports OpenThinker2-32B, trained on public reasoning data, matching DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B on standard reasoning benchmarks.
Develops OpenThinker3-7B using a scaled 1.2M-example pipeline and QwQ-32B as teacher, reporting state-of-the-art benchmark results relative to a specified 7B baseline.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe OpenThinker2-32B as the first model trained on public reasoning data to match DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B on benchmarks such as AIME and LiveCodeBench.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that OpenThinker2-32B matches DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B on AIME and LiveCodeBench.
The authors report that 1,000+ controlled experiments investigating each data-generation step led to OpenThoughts3.

The authors report OpenThinker3-7B scores of 53% on AIME 2025, 51% on LiveCodeBench 06/24–01/25, and 54% on GPQA Diamond—15.3, 17.2, and 20.5 percentage points above DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, respectively.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reasoning models are progressing rapidly, but proprietary training data leaves the best recipes unclear.
OpenThoughts aims to provide open-source datasets for training reasoning models.
OpenThoughts2-1M is reported to support OpenThinker2-32B, matching a named 32B baseline on standard reasoning benchmarks.
The project reports 1,000+ controlled experiments across data-generation steps, producing OpenThoughts3.
A 1.2M-example pipeline with QwQ-32B as teacher yields reported benchmark gains for OpenThinker3-7B; datasets and models are publicly available.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a large set of controlled experiments targeting individual data-generation steps to a subsequent dataset iteration.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests a data-recipe paper can make pipeline choices more interpretable by isolating and testing components before scaling.
lessons.application: Describe the data pipeline as separable decisions, test each decision with controlled comparisons, and use the results to motivate the next recipe revision.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when interventions cannot be isolated or when the evaluation budget is too limited for controlled experimentation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the controlled-experiment designs, datasets, model-training details, or statistical uncertainty.
The reported benchmark comparisons do not state evaluation protocols, contamination controls, or whether all models used equivalent settings.
The abstract alone cannot independently establish the claims of firstness, state-of-the-art status, or benchmark validity.
